prompt: On the unit circle, what is the $y$-coordinate of the point at $60^\circ$? Give the exact value, for example "sqrt(2)/2" for $\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$.

hints.text: Use the $30$-$60$-$90$ triangle: the side opposite $60^\circ$ is $\sqrt{3}$ out of a hypotenuse of $2$.

explanation: On the unit circle, the $y$-coordinate of the point at angle $\theta$ is $\sin \theta$.
So the point at $60^\circ$ is $\left(\frac{1}{2},\ \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)$, and the $y$-coordinate is $\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \approx 0.87$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Does it look right on the circle?
steps: $60^\circ$ is closer to straight up ($90^\circ$) than to the right ($0^\circ$), so the point should be high and not very far right.
$y \approx 0.87$ (high) with $x = 0.5$ (not far right) matches the picture exactly.
